key_insight: Detonation-sprayed Fe-based amorphous coatings can achieve dense, fine-lamellar microstructures that improve corrosion resistance and humidity-dependent wear performance when droplet spreading is optimized.
engineering_relevance: This work guides coating-process tuning for steel protection in corrosive or humid service by linking spray parameters, porosity, and tribological durability.
method: Prepared Fe-based amorphous coatings on Q235 carbon steel by detonation spray under varied parameters.
Compared coating droplet morphology, microstructure density, corrosion behavior, and wear response.
Evaluated tribological performance in different humidity environments using Si3N4 balls.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that coatings with disk-like droplets, higher circularity and expansion factor, and lower porosity showed better long-term corrosion resistance, while friction coefficient and wear rate decreased as humidity increased.
watch_item: Performance depends strongly on porosity and spray condition control, so inconsistent detonation-spray settings could reduce durability and reproducibility.
paper_title: Long-term corrosion behaviors and wear behavior of Fe-based amorphous coatings in different humidity environments
